Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants/claimants assailing the award dated 23.12.2009 passed by the learned District Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Vidisha (M.P.) in Claim Case No.06/2009, whereby the Claims Tribunal exonerated respondent No.3-Insurance Company from its liability to pay compensation and further awarded compensation which, according to the appellants, is inadequate.
Hence, enhancement of compensation has been sought.
2.

entities.text: District Judge, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Vidisha (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The date of accident and issue of negligence are not in dispute.
The findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regard are not in question.

3. As per the findings of the Claims Tribunal in the case of death of Leelabai due to motor accident,
Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:414 2 MA-506-2010 to the tune of Rs.2,60,500/- with interest.

4. The undisputed facts of the case are that on 27.02.2008, deceased Leelabai was travelling from Bhopal to Vidisha on a motorcycle bearing registration No. MP 40 MB 1429 along with Ashok Kumar (non-applicant No.1) and Omprakash (non-applicant No.2).
The motorcycle was being driven by Omprakash.
When the motorcycle reached near Deewanganj Police Outpost, a buffalo suddenly came on the road.

In an attempt to save the animal, the driver lost control and the Suraj Singh @ Golu vs Ashok Kumar on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159362314/
1 motorcycle struck against the road divider, as a result of which all the occupants fell down.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Leelabai sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
The incident was reported to the police, FIR was registered, and after completion of investigation, charge- sheet was filed.

Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the claimants are the children of respondent No.1.
5.
Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the Claims Tribunal has committed a grave error in exonerating the Insurance Company from liability.
It was argued that at the time of the accident, the offending motorcycle was duly insured and therefore the Insurance Company ought to have been directed to satisfy the award.
6. It was further submitted that the compensation awarded is inadequate and on the lower side.

According to the appellants, the deceased was working as a tailor and earning a reasonable income,
which was not properly assessed by the Claims Tribunal.
It was also contended that adequate future prospects were not granted and reasonable compensation under conventional heads such as loss of estate, funeral expenses, etc., was not awarded.
On these grounds, enhancement of compensation and fastening of liability upon the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:414 3 MA-506-2010 Insurance Company was prayed for.

entities.text: NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:414 3 MA-506-2010 Insurance Company
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
7. So far as the controversy involved in the present appeal pertains to the liability of the Insurance Company in respect of the death of a pillion rider of a two-wheeler is concerned, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Sudhakaran K.V. and Others, AIR 2008 SC 2729,
has held that the statutory liability under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act covers the risk of third parties but does not extend to the owner or pillion rider of a two-wheeler unless such risk is specifically covered by the policy.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Sudhakaran K.V. and Others, AIR 2008 SC 2729
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Similarly, in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Shimla v. Tilak Singh and Others, 2006 (II) DMP 147 (SC), it has been held that in the absence of an endorsement such as IMT-70 covering the risk of a pillion rider, the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation for the death of a pillion rider.

entities.text: United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Shimla v. Tilak Singh and Others, 2006 (II) DMP 147 (SC)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In the present case, it is an admitted position that the deceased Leelabai was travelling as a pillion rider on the offending motorcycle.
There is no material on record to show that the insurance policy contained any specific endorsement covering the risk of a pillion rider.
10. In view of the settled position of law and the facts of the case, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Claims Tribunal has rightly exonerated the Insurance Company from liability.
No illegality or perversity is found in the impugned award warranting interference in this regard.

11. So far as the contention of counsel for the claimants with regard to enhancement of compensation is concerned, from perusal of evidence of claimants, it is found that claimants are unable to produce any substantial document with regard to income of the deceased.

So, in view of the judgments NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:414 4 MA-506-2010 in Sukhdevi v.
Devendra Kumar , ILR 2014 MP 172; Kanwar Devi v. Bansal Roadways, 2008 ACJ 2182; and National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Renu Devi , (2008) 3 ACC 134 , when documentary proof of income is Suraj Singh @ Golu vs Ashok Kumar on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159362314/

12. In the present case, the accident occurred on 27.02.2008.
At the relevant time, as per the Minimum Wages Act, the monthly income of an unskilled labourer was Rs. 2,651/- per month.
Therefore, the income of the deceased is required to be assessed at Rs. 2,651/- per month.
Claimant filed the claim petition under Section 163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, therefore, the principles laid down in Sarla Verma and ors.
Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and Anr. reported in (2009) 6 SCC 12 and National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700 are not applicable in this case.

13. Accordingly, appellants- claimants are entitled to get compensation under the following heads:-
 HEAD A  Rs.2651 X 1  Income  31812 per a  After adding Dependency 2/3 Rs.21,208/-
 Rs.2000/- (
 Future prospects  Tribunal)
 Loss of Income Rs.21,208 X  Other Heads (loss of estate, funeral  Rs.2500/-
 expenses etc.)
 Total Compensation 14.

Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.3,43,828/- as against the Award of the Claims Tribunal of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:414 5 MA-506-2010 Rs.2,60,500/-.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the appellants/claimants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.83,328/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
15. In the result, this miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed, by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.83,328/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest as fixed by the learned Claims Tribunal from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The said amount be paid within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
Rest of conditions as imposed by learned Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

16. If the enhanced amount of compensation is in excess to the valuation of appeal, the difference of the Court fee (if not already paid) shall be deposited by the appellants-claimants within a period of one month and proof thereof, shall be submitted before the Registry.
Thereafter, the Registry shall issue the certified copy of the order passed today.
17. In view of the above, miscellaneous appeal filed by the appellants/claimants stands disposed of.
